solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Huge son going to the end, amusing people

indicators.note: the letter for son leaves its place and travels to the back of the word

blocks.note: cosmic means vast, on the scale of the universe
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: An enormous boy heads off to the far end, entertaining everyone on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Take COSMIC, lift out its S and put it at the end: COMIC + S gives COMICS.
explanation.definitionFit: Comics are comedians, people whose job is to make an audience laugh.

clue.text: Small room close to bodega: see red wine store

indicators.note: the close of a word is its finish, so only the final letter of bodega is wanted

blocks.note: a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery
the last letter of bodega
to see red is to be furious, to rage

explanation.surface: A cramped room by the Spanish wine bar where someone fumes over a bottle of red.
explanation.walkthrough: A bodega is a Spanish wine shop, which helps the surface but only lends its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cellarage is cellar space, the storage room where wine is kept below ground.

clue.text: Tower where star has party, right?

blocks.note: Mira is a red giant star in the constellation Cetus
a do is a party
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A celebrity hosts a party in a tower, and the questioner checks that is correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirador is a turret or belvedere tower built to give a commanding view, a Spanish architectural term.

clue.text: Caught he-man in game

blocks.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
Rambo is the musclebound action hero of the Stallone films

explanation.surface: A macho hero is trapped while playing some game.
explanation.definitionFit: Crambo is an old word game in which one player gives a word and others must find rhymes for it.

clue.text: Rubbish outside place, last bit of festive decoration

indicators.note: outside tells us the rubbish word wraps around the place word
the last bit of a word is just its final letter

blocks.note: rot means nonsense, rubbish
to set something is to place it
the final letter of festive

explanation.surface: Rubbish has piled up outside where the final festive decorations hang.
explanation.walkthrough: Place is read as the verb to set, not as a noun for a location.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a ribbon decoration shaped like a rose, as awarded at shows or worn by supporters.

clue.text: Bird — investigating having wings being clipped

indicators.note: a word's wings are its two outer letters, and clipping them trims both away

blocks.note: probing means investigating

explanation.surface: A bird is being examined after having its wings clipped.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the first and last letters of PROBING to leave ROBIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin is a small common songbird with a red breast.

clue.text: Troubled soul, dear Parisian who cannot stand tall?

indicators.note: something troubled is stirred up and disturbed, so its letters are mixed

blocks.note: taken as written for the anagram
cher is French for dear, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: A distressed Frenchman speaks fondly to someone who can never stand up straight.
explanation.walkthrough: Only soul is jumbled; CHER is attached unchanged. The definition reads as 'one who cannot stand tall'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloucher droops and stoops with poor posture, so cannot hold themself upright.

clue.text: Be ill, needing nurse round? The very last thing you want

indicators.note: round says the nurse word surrounds the illness word

blocks.note: to nurse is to tend
to ail is to be ill
surface padding that completes the familiar saying

explanation.surface: Falling sick and needing a nurse to visit is the last thing anyone wants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The very last thing you want' reads as a saying; only its first four words define the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The tail end is the final part of something, the extreme end of a sequence.

clue.text: Number three at sea

indicators.note: something at sea is confused and lost, so the letters are in disorder

blocks.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: The third of something is adrift on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a figure, but read it as 'numb-er', something that numbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether was an early anaesthetic, a substance that deadens feeling, so it is literally a numbing agent.

clue.text: Lincoln bishop with a set of holy books found to be unorthodox

blocks.note: Abe Lincoln, the US president
RR is Right Reverend, a bishop's title
taken as written
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: A bishop of Lincoln owns holy books judged to be heretical.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln suggests the English cathedral city, but it is the president.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberrant means departing from the normal or accepted standard, i.e. deviant or unconventional.

clue.text: Form of life in river covered in flowing liquid?

indicators.note: something covered in another thing is surrounded by it

blocks.note: lava is molten rock that flows out of a volcano
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Asks what sort of life lives in a river of moving water.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva is the immature stage of an insect, one form an animal's life takes before adulthood.

clue.text: Like a monkey's mistake — a blessing being captured

indicators.note: a thing captured is held inside, so the blessing sits within the mistake

blocks.note: bish is British slang for a blunder
a boon is a blessing

explanation.surface: A blunder made by a monkey turns out to be a blessing in disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: Bish is British slang for a blunder. The 's in monkey's is read as 'is' for the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Baboonish describes behaviour resembling a baboon, a large ape-like monkey.

clue.text: Gangster and cleric outside pub — The Star

indicators.note: outside says the cleric word encloses the pub word

blocks.note: Al Capone, the archetypal gangster
a dean is a senior cleric
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A gangster and a priest stand outside a pub named The Star.
explanation.walkthrough: The Star reads like a pub sign, but it is the definition; Al Capone is the standard crossword gangster.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldebaran is the bright red star forming the eye of Taurus, so it is a star by name.

clue.text: Give encouragement to holy person leaving diocese

indicators.note: the holy person departs, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: ST is saint
Chester is an English diocese and cathedral city

explanation.surface: A saint quitting a church district is spurred on.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove ST from CHESTER to leave CHEER.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone is to shout encouragement or lift their spirits.

clue.text: Area of ground that's holy, trimmed at the edges

indicators.note: trimming the edges cuts off the first and final letters

blocks.note: sacred means holy

explanation.surface: A patch of consecrated land neatly mown at its borders.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land area, about 4,047 square metres.

clue.text: Old IT feature fills home-worker with fear

indicators.note: the fear word fills the worker word, sitting inside it

blocks.note: a carer looks after someone in their home
dread is fear

explanation.surface: An outdated computer component terrifies someone working from home.
explanation.walkthrough: Home-worker suggests remote office work, but here it means a care worker who visits people at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A card reader was a device on early computers that read punched cards, a piece of obsolete hardware.

clue.text: Branch of thieves' organisation tried reforming

indicators.note: reforming shapes something anew, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a den of thieves is their lair and gang
taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: A local branch of a criminal gang has attempted to clean up its act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Branch of' reads as part of the surface, but Branch alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dendrite is a branching extension of a nerve cell, or a tree-like crystal formation.

clue.text: Garment covered in grass must be put right

indicators.note: a thing covered in another is wrapped by it on every side

blocks.note: a reed is a tall grass
a dress is a garment

explanation.surface: A dress stained with grass needs to be cleaned up.
explanation.definitionFit: To redress a wrong is to remedy or correct it, so redressed means set right.

clue.text: This person at social function provides food item

blocks.note: the setter referring to themself
taken as written
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: The setter, at a party, hands out something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A meatball is a small ball of minced meat, a common dish.

clue.text: Begging access, endlessly worrying

indicators.note: without an end the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: entry is access
eating, as in what's eating you, means worrying

explanation.surface: Someone pleads anxiously to be let in.
explanation.definitionFit: Entreating is earnestly asking or pleading, a synonym for begging.

clue.text: What's characteristic about conflicting directions in journey?

indicators.note: about places the characteristic word around the direction letters

blocks.note: a trait is a characteristic
north and south are opposite compass points

explanation.surface: Asks what typifies being pulled two ways on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: Conflicting directions are opposite compass points, north and south.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit means passage from one place to another, a trip or crossing.

clue.text: Old man is full of energy? Exactly!

indicators.note: a thing full of something holds it inside

blocks.note: old man is slang for father
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Asks whether father is lively, and agrees emphatically.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead is used for exactly, as in dead right or dead on, so it works as an emphatic exclamation.

clue.text: Attendant always round queen, ready first and last

indicators.note: round puts the always word around the queen letters
the first and the last letters of the word are the only ones kept

blocks.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever
QU is an abbreviation for queen
the first and last letters of ready

explanation.surface: A servant always attends the queen, prepared from start to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: E'er is the poetic form of ever, a common crossword stand-in for always.
explanation.definitionFit: An equerry is an officer who attends a member of the royal family.

clue.text: Duck in second camp: that is flying off

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is flies away, so it is dropped

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a camp or clique is a coterie
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A duck in a second camp: that one is taking off.
explanation.walkthrough: IE is dropped from COTERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoter is a dark-plumaged sea duck.

clue.text: Smallest lake towards where the sun rises

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for lake
the sun rises in the east

explanation.surface: The tiniest lake, lying towards the sunrise.
explanation.definitionFit: Least is the superlative of little, meaning smallest in size or amount.

clue.text: See copper beginning to search place

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is just its opening letter

blocks.note: lo is an old word for see or behold
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
the first letter of search

explanation.surface: A police officer is spotted starting to search somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a police officer, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Locus is Latin for place, used for a particular position or site.

clue.text: Safety device could make car heat up

indicators.note: could make says the letters can be formed into something new

blocks.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: A safety gadget might cause a car to overheat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heat up' looks like a phrasal verb, but up is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A parachute slows a fall from an aircraft, a device to keep someone safe.

clue.text: Reminder about being associated with people posh and arrogant

indicators.note: about has the reminder word wrapped around the next piece

blocks.note: a prod is a nudge or reminder
U denotes upper-class usage, the speech of posh people

explanation.surface: A prompt about mixing with upper-class people who are snobbish.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes inside PROD. U, from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U, marks upper-class language.
explanation.definitionFit: Proud can mean haughty, having too high an opinion of oneself.

clue.text: Search all the players before a session

blocks.note: the cast is all the actors in a play
taken as written
a bout is a session or spell of activity

explanation.surface: The full company of actors hunts around ahead of a rehearsal.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast about is to look around in all directions for something, to hunt.

clue.text: Look hard, one side to the other, for weeds

indicators.note: a letter at one side of the word is lifted off and moved across to the opposite side

blocks.note: to stare is to look hard

explanation.surface: Gazing intently across a field searching for weeds.
explanation.walkthrough: Move the S of STARE from the front to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Tares are weeds among grain, as in the biblical parable of the wheat and the tares.

clue.text: Decided to add modern light to beastly home

blocks.note: a sett is a badger's burrow
an LED is a light-emitting diode, a modern bulb

explanation.surface: Someone resolved to install new lighting in an animal shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue writes LED first but it goes at the end of SETT.
explanation.definitionFit: A settled matter has been decided or resolved.

clue.text: Class reportedly got older and wiser?

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so what is spoken stands for the word

blocks.note: a grade is a class or rank

explanation.surface: A school year apparently grew up and learnt something.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition: grey hair suggests age and wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair turns grey with age, and grey heads are proverbially wise, so greyed fits by example.
